lens: all three in turn (learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate); scores are the mean of the three passes

gates.G3_broken_graph: pass (nodes S1.case to END read; every next resolves to a node and every non-END node has a way forward; validate not run because this judge has no shell)

rationale.R1: Most new ideas open with a probe: S1.case, S1.pain, S1.first_test, S2.start, S2.c3, S2.c5, S3.open, S3.tg_a, S4.case_a, S5.fit_plan, S6.asym, S7.p1, S8.p1. Exceptions tell first: S2.c2 and S2.c4 explain before their probes; S3.contrast and S4.contrast_read explain before the next probe.
rationale.R2: Traps are real and mapped to the trap map, with tempting-then-refute feedback on most wrong options (S1.case_t4, S3.open_waves, S4.case_b_t_mrcp, S6.h_t1, S8.p10_t0). Losses: several keys are findable by form (S3.cv_a, S3.cv_b, S5.grade_vignette, S7.p9, S7.p10, S2.c4q); several 'partial' options carry no trap (S1.case, S1.pain, S1.sens); S2.c4q haemolysis and cirrhosis options are tagged TR15 but test a risk-factor confusion, not the black-brown swap; many feedback nodes open with the same stock line.
rationale.R3: All 12 objectives are probed on the main path and on the fast lane (S6.fast then S6.fast_o9 then S6.h). O2 and O9 have two or more probes each. Depth is right for O4, O5, O8 and O10.
rationale.R4: Most nodes are one idea and short. Overloads: S5.grade3_teach and S5.numbers_iii_why each list six organ thresholds in two messages, and the two overlap. S3.sign_explain stacks four clues. Several sure_note texts repeat the feedback body nearly word for word (S7.p4_t1, S7.p4_t2, S7.p5_t1, S7.p6_t1, S7.p8_t3).
rationale.R5: Real fast lanes (S6.gate to S6.fast; skips at S1.case_ok, S3.open_ok, S3.cv_b_ok, S4.case_b_ok, S5.grade_ok). Hint ladder on nearly every key probe (hint, retry, then explanation), sure_note confidence prompts, and second explanations in new forms (S3.open_side, S3.tg_sets, S5.grade_why, S5.numbers_why, S5.retest_t11a to S5.c_case, S6.asym_why). Loss: most 'Show me why' branches go forward without re-asking the item.
rationale.R6: PYQ key and current practice are taught both ways (S2.c8_ok, S5.fit_t11a, S7.p10_ok, S8.p4_ok). Exam forms are drilled: first versus most accurate (S1.first_test, S1.sens), 'which is NOT part of the pentad' (S8.p7), TG18 numbers (S5.numbers_ii, S5.numbers_iii, S8.p1). Loss: a few keys are guessable by form, which an examiner would notice.
rationale.R7: Decisions are real clinical moments: the 42-year-old with RUQ pain (S1.case), the 34-year-old with two-day pain (S5.grade_vignette), the ventilated ICU patient with a distended gallbladder (S6.e), the day-six ICU patient on noradrenaline (S8.p11), the drain with green bile on day two (S8.p9), the bail-out at laparoscopy (S6.bail).
rationale.R8: Warm and direct, addresses 'you', no ability praise, no controlling words. But the stock 'That choice is not right.' opens almost every wrong tap and 'You were sure, so ...' opens most sure notes. Over the long S8 run this reads as a template. Persona sim engagement was 3 of 5.
rationale.R9: Most probes separate one wrong model from the right one (colic by duration, first versus most accurate, black versus brown, Courvoisier qualifiers, TG18 sets, critical view order), so the path alone says a lot about what a learner believes. Losses: 'partial' options carry no trap, and the rendered report reads first attempts only (see r9_reports).

segments.reason: Probe-first hook with trap-mapped options (TR4, TR2) and tempting-then-refute feedback. Losses: partial fillers at S1.case (Choledocholithiasis), S1.pain (two-day pain option) and S1.sens (CT); S1.sens_why and S1.case_why go forward without re-asking the probe.

S2.c4q key is the longest option and the only one matching the cholesterol profile; its haemolysis and cirrhosis distractors are tagged TR15 but test a risk-factor confusion. S2.c8 (PYQ key, teach both) is the best node in the module, but S2.c5 and S2.c6 repeat the same acalculous idea in two forms without a bridge.

Patient A and B contrast (S3.open) with a real side-by-side fallback that re-asks (S3.open_side then S3.open); TG18 ladder S3.tg_a, S3.tg_b, S3.tg_c with retries. Losses: S3.cv_a and S3.cv_b keys are the longest option and the only one with the qualifier; S3.sign_explain stacks four clues.

Case-based ladder: first test (S4.case_a), confirmatory HIDA (S4.case_b), duct test (S4.case_c), TG18 sets (S4.case_d). Every wrong test is tied to its job (S4.case_b_t_mrcp, S4.case_c_t_ercp) and retries are offered. Loss: S4.case_d key is the only 'A, B and C' option.

Grade then timing with a real retest: S5.fit_retest is a fresh form, and S5.retest_t11a to S5.c_case is a case-based second explanation. Losses: S5.grade_vignette has two Grade II distractors and one Grade I key, so the key is found by form; S5.grade3_teach and S5.numbers_iii_why repeat the six organ thresholds.

Fast lane (S6.gate) and clean qualifier cases: S6.asym_why (a hundred people) and S6.h_why / S6.i_why (critical view as a checklist) are strong. Losses: S6.b key is the only non-stone option; the S6.fast_why and S6.f_why explanations go forward without a re-ask.

Many trap retests land on an explanation and then move on (S7.p1_show, S7.p2_show, S7.p3_show, S7.p6_show, S7.p7_show, S7.p9_show), so the in-walk recovery is not tested. sure_note text duplicates the feedback body (S7.p4_t1, S7.p5_t1, S7.p8_t3). S7.p10 key is the only non-operating option, and S7.p10_ok, S7.p10_t1 and S7.p10_show carry a node-level flag 'unverified'.

Consolidation runs eleven probes (p1 to p12, no p5) with feedback only between them; this is most of the 220-step walk and the thread is lost. Cold probes p7 to p11 are right in design, but there is no bridge line, and 'Show the answer' exits forward without re-asking. S8.p3 key is the only option naming contrast.

misconceived.report.json.verdict: partly accurate; right on calibration and card order, wrong on recovery
misconceived.report.json.accurate: calibration overconfident and sure_wrong 49 match the walk; the card order and 'do the O-card' pointers are actionable; the trap text 'meet it again on a fresh question' is the right next step.
misconceived.report.json.inaccurate: headline weak and all 12 objectives gap come from first attempts only, though the walk corrected most traps on retry; 18 traps are fell_open although the walk recovered them on retry (TR3, TR4, TR7, TR11, TR14, TR20, TR23, TR24 among them); hints 29 counts explanation taps, not hints; cold_right 2 of 10 is not explained.

merge_ideas: Give every 'Show me why' branch the S3.open_side pattern: explanation, then a return to the same probe in a new form, so that a second miss is tested rather than passed.
Replace each 'partial' option with a trap-map distractor (or drop it), so every wrong tap diagnoses one model (S1.case, S1.pain, S1.sens first).
Shuffle option length on the keys flagged in flaws (S3.cv_a, S3.cv_b, S2.c4q, S7.p9, S7.p10) so the key is not the longest or the odd one out.
Use one organ-threshold teaching node (S5.grade3_teach) and let S5.numbers_iii_why explain only the Grade III logic; remove the duplicate list.
Break the S8 run into two blocks of five or six probes with a one-line bridge each, and re-ask the earliest trap of each block (e.g. TR2 before S8.p3, TR11 before S8.p4).
notes: Factual accuracy not judged (knowledge-only mode). Judged from module.json (all nodes read), report.json, sim/misconceived.md and sim/misconceived.report.json.
